system_description.narrative_title: AI boom reshaping economy, security, and supply chains
system_description.narrative_summary: Across this news window a single dominant narrative threads rapid AI-driven investment and product deployment with rising systemic risk and geopolitical tension. The system is open: capital, data, talent, and hardware flow across firms, markets, and borders while AI models and agents change attack surfaces, regulatory questions, labor demand, and industrial supply chains. Feedbacks include investment amplifying chip and cloud demand (which drives more investment), AI agents creating new cyber vulnerabilities (which spur security markets and insurance changes), and geopolitical competition over semiconductor capacity and AI talent intensifying policy responses. The outcome space is highly path-dependent and fragile to shocks (cyber incidents, supply bottlenecks, regulatory shifts).
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: AI models and agent deployments, cloud and chip providers, startups and incumbents, investors and financial markets, cybersecurity actors (criminal and defensive), insurers, regulators and courts, labor/skills shifts, and manufacturing/supply chains (semiconductors, memory, hardware).
system_description.super_system: Global political-economy-technology ecosystem (geopolitics, finance, trade, and international regulation).
adjacent_subsystems: Labor markets and social policy / regulation

variables.name: AI deployment intensity
variables.description: The aggregate pervasiveness and scale of deployed AI models and autonomous agents across economic sectors and applications.

variables.name: Compute capacity supply
variables.description: The available processing power (cloud, edge, and on-premises) that can be allocated to AI training and inference workloads.

variables.name: AI investment flow
variables.description: The rate of capital deployment into AI-related R&D, startups, infrastructure, and productization.

variables.name: Chip production capacity
variables.description: The manufacturing throughput and producible volume of semiconductors, accelerators, and memory used for AI hardware.

variables.name: Chip supply-chain resilience
variables.description: The ability of semiconductor and hardware supply chains to absorb disruptions and maintain timely delivery of components.

variables.name: Talent pool skill density
variables.description: The concentration of workers with relevant AI skills and experience relative to demand across industries.

variables.name: Data availability and flow rate
variables.description: The volume, accessibility, and velocity of data streams available for AI training, fine-tuning, and operational use.

variables.name: Model opacity level
variables.description: The average interpretability, explainability, and transparency of deployed AI models and decision agents.

variables.name: Cybersecurity vulnerability surface
variables.description: The aggregate exposure and attack surface created by AI integrations, agents, APIs, and connected hardware.

variables.name: Cyberattack incidence rate
variables.description: The frequency of successful or reported cyber incidents that exploit AI-related vectors or targets.

variables.name: Insurance coverage availability
variables.description: The breadth, depth, and affordability of insurance products covering cyber and AI-enabled operational risks.

variables.name: Regulatory stringency
variables.description: The strictness, scope, and enforcement intensity of laws, standards, and regulatory oversight applicable to AI and related tech.

variables.name: Legal accountability clarity
variables.description: The clarity and predictability of liability rules, legal responsibility, and judicial interpretation for AI-driven harms.

variables.name: Valuation volatility
variables.description: The variability and sensitivity of market valuations and investor sentiment tied to AI narratives, earnings, and forecasts.

variables.name: Automation pressure
variables.description: The economic and technological incentive intensity to substitute human labor with AI-driven automation across tasks and roles.

variables.name: Geopolitical competition intensity
variables.description: The degree of interstate strategic competition over access to AI-relevant resources, production capacity, and talent.

catalysts.title: Nvidia's bullish guidance and revenue-policy shift
catalysts.description: Nvidia's very large revenue forecast and pause of revenue-sharing with cloud partners will reshape cloud economics and investor flows into AI infrastructure and software.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Nvidia forecasts 70% sales growth fuelled by relentless AI boom"; "Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies, WSJ reports"; "Nvidia Reports Blowout Quarter"

catalysts.title: Large memory and fab investment wave
catalysts.description: Announcements of multibillion-dollar investments by Kioxia/SanDisk and SK Hynix's U.S. facility point to accelerated capital spend to expand memory and fab capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Kioxia, Sandisk to invest over $31 billion in Japan amid AI boom"; "SK Hynix CEO says Indiana will be key memory production base by 2030, first U.S. facility now underway"

catalysts.title: Andreessen Horowitz 'Machine Age' fund deployment
catalysts.description: The newly launched ‘Machine Age’ fund will direct venture capital toward AI supply-chain and infrastructure bottlenecks, accelerating startups and hardware initiatives.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Exclusive | Andreessen Horowitz Launches ‘Machine Age’ Fund to Tackle AI Supply Bottlenecks"

catalysts.title: Escalation of AI-enabled cyberattacks
catalysts.description: A cluster of incidents and reports showing AI-assisted hacks, plus exploited tools, point to a near-term rise in AI-driven cyber incidents and attack sophistication.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Cyber attack on UK’s largest airport group exposes data..."; "OpenAI says it took a week to detect its AI models had hacked Hugging Face"; "AI’s hacking capabilities are severely underestimated"; "Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies"

catalysts.title: Private sector AI cyber-defense surge
catalysts.description: A coalition of firms signing onto a major defensive initiative will mobilize standards, tooling, and shared detection, reducing some attack success and raising insurer interest.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "'We have a limited window': 116 companies, entities sign on to major AI cyber defense push"; "Major tech companies call for defensive surge to defeat AI-driven hacks"

catalysts.title: Anthropic expands agent control of physical devices
catalysts.description: Anthropic's new framework and experiment-capable tool broaden agents' ability to operate physical systems and scientific apparatus, raising deployment and safety questions.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Anthropic unveils new framework allowing AI agents to operate physical devices"; "Anthropic launches AI tool that can conduct scientific experiments"

catalysts.title: Apple September product event
catalysts.description: Apple's early-September event may introduce AI-enabled device/software updates and subscription pricing that shift consumer AI deployment and software-sector valuations.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "What's expected at Apple's September event — plus, an uneven rally in AI stocks"; "Apple hikes subscription prices for Apple TV and Apple One in the U.S."

catalysts.title: Tech CEOs to speak at G20 tech meeting
catalysts.description: High-profile CEO participation at a tech-focused G20 session could catalyze international policy signals and coordination on AI safety, trade, and security.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "OpenAI, Nvidia CEOs to speak at tech-focused G20 meeting"

catalysts.title: OpenAI ends model access to SpaceX-owned Cursor
catalysts.description: OpenAI's move to cut off model access to Cursor after SpaceX acquisition will disrupt an integration and could spur private feuds, forks, or alternative access routes.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "OpenAI to end model access to Cursor after acquisition by Elon Musk's SpaceX"; "OpenAI to cut off AI models for SpaceX-owned Cursor, escalating feud with Musk"
